title: The Blue Whale
seo_title: Whale Charcuterie Board: Blueberry Showpiece & Shopping List
description: A blue whale charcuterie board for 12 to 15: a whale made mostly of blueberries and blackberries, with a cheese belly, swimming through salami and cheese.
hook: A giant whale swimming across a sea of food, its body made of blueberries and blackberries.

items.name: Small block of cheese to hold the spout

why: This is one of the easiest showpieces in the book, because the whale is mostly berries: pour them into the outline and the shape appears. White cheddar or provolone slices make the striped belly, and a mozzarella eye finishes the face.
Around the whale, salami and prosciutto roses, chilled shrimp, blue cheese, brie and cubed cheese make the ocean. It suits beach birthdays, baby showers and summer parties.

timeline.what: Draw and cut the whale template, slice the cheese belly strips, and peel the cucumber ribbons (store them in cold water).
Lay the belly stripes and fill the whale with berries.
Add the spout and the eye, then fill the sea.
Add the shrimp from the fridge.

faq.q: How do you make a whale charcuterie board?
faq.a: Outline the whale shape, fill the body with blueberries and blackberries, lay thin cheese slices for the belly and add a mozzarella eye. Fill the rest of the board with meat roses, shrimp and cheese.
It's rated 2 of 5 in the book, one of the easiest showpieces, and takes about 75 minutes.

Wash and dry the berries and make the meat roses the day before. Keep meat, cheese and cut fruit out no more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F. For a long party, build half, keep the refill in the fridge and top it up halfway through.
